title_en: Brad Gerstner & Geoffrey Canada - Raising the Floor for Every American Child - [Invest Like the Best, EP.501]
title_zh: Brad Gerstner 与 Geoffrey Canada：为每一个美国孩子抬高底线（Invest Like the Best EP.501）
subtitle_zh: Brad Gerstner 与 Geoffrey Canada 解读《Invest America Act》：为每个美国孩子开设 $1,000 资本账户，用复利把美国梦交回穷人手中。
summary_zh: 本集由主持人 Patrick O'Shaughnessy 对话投资人 Brad Gerstner 与 Harlem Children's Zone 创始人 Geoffrey Canada，围绕 2025 年 7 月 4 日签署成法的《Invest America Act》展开。该法案为每个在美国出生的孩子自动开设账户，注入 $1,000 投资于 S&P 500，被称为“全民资本账户”或 Trump accounts（530A 账户）。Geoffrey 从五十年反贫困经历出发，指出教育是机会平等的关键，但没有资本，穷孩子“距离破产只差一场意外”，代际财富长期绕过了美国穷人。Brad 则从“冷启动问题”讲起，解释为何必须自动开户、自动注资，并引入 Michael 与 Susan Dell、Elon Musk 等慈善家的直接捐赠。两人认为，让每个家庭都“拥有一点点 Apple、Berkshire”，能重建人们对资本主义的信任。节目还谈及 AI 与就业冲击，Brad 引用 Keynes 1930 年的判断，把全民资本账户比作 AI 时代的 Social Security。

turns.en: are thinking about this technology? I think we have to address this one specifically because it is a wave of wealth creation, of obviously people are very against it in certain ways. I had a session with some of my young folks. And I asked them, what have you heard?
turns.zh: 他们是怎么看待这项技术的？我认为我们必须专门谈一谈这个，因为它是一波财富创造的浪潮，而显然人们在某些方面非常反对它。我跟一些我带的年轻人开了一场会。我问他们，你们听到了什么？

turns.en: Have you heard? It's going to kill us all.
turns.zh: 你们有没有听到，它会把我们全都害死？

turns.en: Have you heard, it's going to take all of our jobs? Have you heard that it's going to make life better?
turns.zh: 你们有没有听到，它会夺走我们所有的工作？你们有没有听到，它会让生活变得更美好？

turns.en: No, so they're a bunch of folk who are thinking in medicine and hell, oh, this is, so it's going to be incredible. But when the leaders of the companies are saying, oh, yeah, by the way, there's some chance it'll kill us all, I bet. So that, that, you begin to wonder, and I think this is happening across the world right now.
turns.zh: 没有。所以，他们是一群（想着）学医之类的人，想的是，哦，这会……所以它会不可思议。但当这些公司的领导人在说，哦，是啊，顺便说一句，有那么点可能它会把我们全都害死——我敢打赌（他们就只听到这个）。所以，那，你就会开始琢磨，而我认为这正在全世界发生。

turns.en: You begin to wonder, is someone taking a risk with my life and my family's life so they can make a whole bunch of money? Is that what this really is? I don't know, any young folks will think this thing is great. Oh, I can't wait. I just think this is going it. They're hearing all of the downside of this.
turns.zh: 你就会开始琢磨，是不是有人正在拿我的生命、我家人的生命去冒险，好让他们能赚一大堆钱？这难道就是这件事的真相吗？我不知道，（哪个）年轻人会觉得这个东西很棒。哦，我等不及了。我只是觉得这会……他们听到的全是这件事的负面。

turns.en: And they're seeing the ripple effects, you know, as folks announce layoffs of jobs and other thoughts and folks are thinking, this thing is just beginning. So I worry, I worry, I think that you're seeing this pushback against data centers and other things around the country as folks are starting to say, what is this whole thing all about?
turns.zh: 而他们正看到那些连锁反应，你知道，随着各家宣布裁员之类的事情，人们就在想，这个东西才刚刚开始。所以我担心，我担心。我认为，你正在看到全国各地对数据中心和其他东西的这种抵制，因为人们开始说，这整件事到底是为了什么？

turns.en: And there is so much good that can come out of this. The conversation, and I've asked folks privately, the conversation, once you say something like, maybe it might kill us all. It's hard to have another conversation if, now maybe I kill us all, but I'm giving you 20 million. Okay, I'm good with that. I'll take my risk, all right?
turns.zh: 而这里面能产生如此之多的好处。这场对话——我私下问过人们——这场对话，一旦你说出像'也许它可能把我们全都害死'这样的话，就很难再展开另一场对话了。如果是'现在，也许它会害死我们所有人，但我给你 2,000 万'。好吧，我接受。我冒这个险，好吗？

turns.en: Maybe it might kill us all, I'm giving you nothing. Yeah, exactly. That's a problem. I would say to the folks who are driving this, that if they really want to get this generation engaged, they need to make sure that the risk and reward, it's not all risk. There's some reward coming from this.
turns.zh: '也许它可能把我们全都害死，可我什么都不给你。'是啊，没错。那就是个问题。我想对推动这一切的那些人说，如果他们真的想让这一代人参与进来，他们就得确保风险与回报（是平衡的）——不能全是风险。得有一些回报从中产生。

turns.en: And that's where I think these accounts could really be helpful because at least you're in the game. I'm in the game with you. We're taking risk with everybody's getting some reward right now, right now for poor people. It's all risk. Remember, just two weeks ago, anthropic announced, you know, their foundation, their philanthropic arm,
turns.zh: 而这，正是我认为这些账户可能真正有帮助的地方，因为至少你参与了这场游戏。我和你一起在这场游戏里。我们一起承担风险，每个人现在都能得到一些回报——眼下，对穷人来说，全是风险。记住，就在两周前，Anthropic 宣布了，你知道，他们的基金会、他们的慈善部门，

turns.en: and when they announced it on Twitter, they said the money's gonna go to two places. One place is traditional charities that are dealing with things that can help ameliorate any of these concerns. They said the second place is direct citizen accounts. Well, the only direct citizen accounts I know are these 530A accounts.
turns.zh: 而当他们在 Twitter 上宣布时，他们说这笔钱会流向两个地方。一个是传统的慈善机构，处理那些能帮助缓解任何这些担忧的事情。他们说，第二个地方是'直接的公民账户'。嗯，我所知道的唯一'直接的公民账户'，就是这些 530A 账户。

turns.en: And Elon responded to that and said, put it into the 530A accounts. Then he said, that's what I'm doing. And shortly thereafter, he's gonna give shares of SpaceX to every kid in the country. You're absolutely right. They have to feel like they own part of anthropic and open AI and SpaceX. And not only feel that way,
turns.zh: 而 Elon 对此回应说，把钱放进 530A 账户里。然后他说，这正是我要做的。此后不久，他就将把 SpaceX 的股份给这个国家的每一个孩子。你说得完全正确。他们必须感觉到，自己拥有 Anthropic、OpenAI 和 SpaceX 的一部分。而且不只是感觉那样，

turns.en: they actually have to own it and share in the upside. I'm quite confident that technological progress is going to bring benefits for everybody's gonna grow the economy that will outweigh the downside. But we gotta walk people across this bridge, right? And when we have activists and other people like Caxden
turns.zh: 他们实际上必须拥有它，并分享那份上升收益。我相当确信，技术进步将会给每个人带来好处、将会推动经济增长，其益处会超过弊端。但我们必须带着人们走过这座'桥'，对吧？而当我们有活动人士、以及其他像 Caxden（Zohran Mamdani）这样的人，

turns.en: come out and say 10% chance it can kill everybody. Remember, we shut down 47 nuclear reactors, fission reactors in this country for similar fears and concerns. But can I do, doldge me for a second? Because I've been studying this 1930, okay? 1930, we have 22% unemployment in America.
turns.zh: 出来说'有 10% 的可能它会害死所有人'时。记住，出于类似的恐惧和担忧，我们关停了这个国家的 47 座核反应堆、裂变反应堆。但我能……让我打断你一下好吗？因为我一直在研究这个——1930 年，好吗？1930 年，我们 America 的失业率是 22%。

turns.en: And people were panicked about the industrial revolution that machines were going to replace jobs. We think we have a problem in this country today. We have 4.1% unemployment. So here are the words that Cain said that I think are pretty prophetic. He wrote an essay you can look it up called economic possibilities for our grandchildren.
turns.zh: 而人们对工业革命感到恐慌，担心机器会取代工作。我们觉得今天我们在这个国家有个问题。我们的失业率是 4.1%。所以，这里是 Keynes 说过的一些话，我认为颇具预言性。他写了一篇文章，你可以去查，叫《我们孙辈的经济前景》（Economic Possibilities for Our Grandchildren）。

turns.en: So Cain's was watching Europe come apart at the seams, was tilting towards socialism or communism, fascism was developing in Europe. Does that sound familiar? Paris on fire, okay? That was happening in 1930. Cain's was profoundly worried about that for the United States. And so he wanted to make the case that things may be
turns.zh: 所以，Keynes 当时正看着 Europe 分崩离析、正倒向社会主义或共产主义，法西斯主义正在 Europe 发展。这听起来耳熟吗？Paris 在燃烧，好吗？那正在 1930 年发生。Keynes 对此为 United States 深感担忧。所以他想论证：事情也许在短期内会

turns.en: hard in the short term, but stick with the industrial revolution because it will make you far wealthier in the long term. And here's what he said. He said for the moment, the very rapidity of these changes is hurting us and bringing a difficult problem to solve. We are being afflicted with a new disease
turns.zh: 很难，但要坚持工业革命，因为它从长远看会让你富有得多。而这是他说的话。他说，'眼下，这些变化之迅速本身正在伤害我们，并带来一个难以解决的问题。我们正被一种新疾病所困扰，

turns.en: of which some readers may not have yet heard the name, but of which they will hear a great deal in the years to come, namely technological unemployment. I mean, he coined the phrase, technological unemployment in 1930 because we were mechanized means of production. He says, but this is only a temporary phase.
turns.zh: 一些读者也许还没听过它的名字，但在未来几年他们会大量听到它——那就是技术性失业（technological unemployment）。'我是说，他在 1930 年就创造了'技术性失业'这个说法，因为我们当时（正经历）机械化的生产方式。他说，但这只是一个暂时的阶段。

turns.en: I would predict that the standard of life in progressive countries, 100 years hence will be between four and eight times as high as it is today. So he was saying, stick with it people. Stick with it. Don't give up on technological progress. It will make us all wealthier. It will improve all of our lives.
turns.zh: '我会预测，进步国家的生活水平，在此后 100 年，将会是今天的四到八倍。'所以他是说，坚持下去，各位。坚持下去。不要放弃技术进步。它会让我们所有人都更富有。它会改善我们所有人的生活。

turns.en: But if we abandon it right now for fascism, we lose everything. We're on the 100th anniversary, right? 2030 is the 100th anniversary of this. And how much bigger do you think our economy is than it was when he wrote this, 8.2 times? Wow. Okay, crazy. His forecast, we just topped the high end of his forecast. People are living longer.
turns.zh: 但如果我们现在为了法西斯主义而抛弃它，我们就会失去一切。我们正处在这（篇文章）的 100 周年纪念，对吧？2030 年是它的 100 周年纪念。而你觉得，我们的经济体比他写这篇文章时大了多少？8.2 倍。哇。好。太疯狂了。他的预测——我们刚刚超过了那个预测的上限。人们活得更久了。

turns.en: Everybody has more than they did in 1930. I mean, it may be challenging today, but it's better than it was in 1930. And so you look at this on almost every dimension human progress has taken us to a better place. But 1930, nobody could have ever envisioned the jobs that we have today. 80% of the jobs that we have today
turns.zh: 每个人拥有的都比 1930 年多。我是说，今天也许充满挑战，但比 1930 年要好。所以，你几乎从每一个维度来看，人类的进步都把我们带到了一个更好的地方。但在 1930 年，没人能想象出我们今天拥有的这些工作。我们今天拥有的工作中，有 80%

turns.en: did not exist in 1930. And so we're in this moment again, where we have to trust the technological progress is going to bring us to a better place. I know deep down that it will, but we have to build a bridge to take people on that journey. The bridge this country passed in 1935 was social security.
turns.zh: 在 1930 年并不存在。所以我们又一次处在这个时刻：我们必须信任，技术进步会把我们带到一个更好的地方。我内心深处知道它会，但我们必须建一座'桥'，带人们走完那段旅程。这个国家在 1935 年通过的那座'桥'，就是 social security。

turns.en: So Keynes was saying, change the social contract to keep democracy together, to keep capitalism together. What was the number one asset people had in 1935? They're labor. They didn't own things. They had their labor. So we said, if you're unemployed, we will give you unemployment compensation.
turns.zh: 所以，Keynes 是在说，改变社会契约，以维系民主、维系资本主义。1935 年人们拥有的头号资产是什么？是他们的劳动力。他们不拥有东西。他们拥有自己的劳动力。所以我们说，如果你失业了，我们会给你失业补偿。

turns.en: When you retire, we will give you compensation. Social security was an unheard of social contract around the world in 1935. But we passed it, and it paved the way for a hundred years of progress for this country. I think that the Invest America Act of 2025 will be to the age of AI, universal capital accounts.
turns.zh: 当你退休时，我们会给你补偿。Social security 在 1935 年是一项全世界闻所未闻的社会契约。但我们通过了它，它为这个国家此后一百年的进步铺平了道路。我认为，2025 年的 Invest America Act、以及全民资本账户，之于 AI 时代，

turns.en: What the Social Security Act was to the industrial age. It kept the country together. It got everybody into the game. It gave everybody the security to say, okay, I'll trust you on this. I'll go down this path, because I know I'm also benefiting, right? And we're gonna need that Patrick to get to the place, right?
turns.zh: 就如同 Social Security Act 之于工业时代。它让这个国家凝聚在一起。它让每个人都参与到这场游戏里。它给了每个人那种安全感，去说，好，这件事我信你。我会走这条路，因为我知道我自己也在受益，对吧？而我们需要那个，Patrick，才能走到那个地方，对吧？

turns.en: We know we're going to displace jobs, right? It's impossible to believe that we're not gonna displace any jobs. But to get to the age of abundance that Silicon Valley loves to talk about, right? We need to take everybody on that journey. It's gonna take a bit. And this is what I have said to my young folks.
turns.zh: 我们知道我们将会取代一些工作，对吧？要相信我们不会取代任何工作，是不可能的。但要抵达那个 Silicon Valley 爱谈论的'丰饶时代'，对吧？我们需要带上每一个人一起走那段旅程。这会需要一点时间。而这，就是我一直跟我那些年轻人说的话。

turns.en: Like it or not, it ain't going away. We've got to figure out what does that mean for us. And I would say to all of those folks who are going to benefit in ways that probably can create more wealth for more folks than we've ever seen before. If you care about your country, you will make sure that that wealth
turns.zh: 不管你喜欢与否，它都不会消失。我们得搞清楚，那对我们意味着什么。而我想对所有那些将会以各种方式受益的人说——他们能创造的财富，也许会比我们以往见过的、为更多人创造的都多——如果你在乎你的国家，你就会确保那份财富

turns.en: gets shared in some way that makes American stink we're all one people. And some of us aren't taking advantage of others and risking other people's lives because we wanna make a whole bunch of money. That, to me, is what's being set up right now just with the conversation. And I think one of the answers is to say,
turns.zh: 以某种方式得到分享，让美国人觉得，我们都是一个民族，让我们中的一些人不去占别人的便宜、不去拿别人的生命冒险，只为自己想赚一大堆钱。那，对我来说，正是眼下（仅凭）这场对话就在被搭建起来的局面。而我认为，答案之一就是去说，

turns.en: no, we are investing in your young people. We are part of the solution. And we're all on this journey together. Yes, there's the risk, but there's rewards for everybody. Can you say just a word about the people that you've worked with at Blue Meridian and elsewhere and their desires? Part of the problem seems to be
turns.zh: 不，我们正在投资你们的年轻人。我们是解决方案的一部分。我们都在这段旅程上一起。是的，有风险，但回报属于每一个人。你能不能就用一句话谈谈，你在 Blue Meridian 和其他地方合作过的那些人，以及他们的愿望？问题的一部分似乎是，

turns.en: this us versus them kind of mentality and the sort of fat cat would be the term that people used to use that are getting enriched by this technology and by other technologies historically. But both the companies, SpaceX giving a share, you know, I'm giving a share to everybody andthropic maybe doing something similar.
turns.zh: 这种'我们 vs 他们'的心态，还有那种——'fat cat'（大肥猫）是人们过去常用的词——那些靠这项技术、以及历史上靠其他技术发财的人。但无论是公司，比如 SpaceX 给出一股，你知道，'我给每个人一股'，Anthropic 也许也在做类似的事。

turns.en: Like, bring us into the room a little bit with like, I will tell you, at Blue Meridian Partners, we have a group of philanthropists who are interested in how much money they can give away right now. And they're doing it all. Not when they die, they're not pledging to someone. They are saying, I am wealthy and I know America has challenges
turns.zh: 就像，给我们讲讲，让我们稍微'进到现场'了解一下。我会告诉你，在 Blue Meridian Partners，我们有一群慈善家，他们关心的是'我现在能捐出多少钱'。而且他们正在把钱全都捐出去。不是等他们死了才捐，也不是向某人承诺。他们是在说，'我很富有，我知道 America 有各种挑战，

turns.en: and I want to partner with other folks to not do small things, but to do big things with philanthropy. So our average grand size is somewhere between $1,500 million we're trying to scale things that work across the country. Yes, you know, there's a thing like billionaires and they like the new, you know, evil people in the world,
turns.zh: 我想和其他人一起合作，不是做小事情，而是用 philanthropy 做大事。'所以，我们的平均捐赠规模在 $1,500（万）左右。我们试图把那些行之有效的东西在全国范围内规模化。是啊，你知道，有这么个东西叫亿万富翁，他们就像是新出现的、你知道，世界上的'坏人'，

turns.en: all the poor people I know want to be billionaires. I don't know one poor person who says, oh, I hate billionaires, they're all like, how did they do it? How can I, and I'm being honest, how can I get there, right? Because they want to be successful, they want to be wealthy. I know that right now,
turns.zh: 可我认识的所有穷人都想成为亿万富翁。我不认识哪个穷人会说，'哦，我讨厌亿万富翁'，他们都（想），'他们是怎么做到的？我怎样才能……'我说实话，'我怎样才能到那个位置？'对吧？因为他们想要成功，他们想要富有。我知道，眼下

turns.en: there is an opportunity to have the biggest investments in the social sector that we probably had in the history of this country. And I don't think the folks I'm working with are not doing it because suddenly, it's become a dirty work for the last 10 years. They have quietly been trying to figure out how do we get this money out the door.
turns.zh: 正有一个机会，能对社会领域进行也许是这个国家历史上最大规模的投资。而我并不认为，我合作的那些人没去做这件事，是因为在过去 10 年里它突然变成了一个'脏词'。他们一直在悄悄地设法搞清楚，我们该怎么把这些钱花出去。

turns.en: It is, this is how it's funny, but when my billionaire friends tell me this, it's really hard to give away money, right? Like, not that hard, give it to me, I'll give it away, I'll give it away, right? But what it turns out to make smart investments because we haven't scaled the sector, you can overwhelm an organization,
turns.zh: 这，这很好笑，但当我的亿万富翁朋友们告诉我，'把钱捐出去真的很难'，对吧？就像，不是说那么难啦——给我，我来帮你捐，我会把它捐出去的，对吧？但事实证明，要做出明智的投资，因为这个领域还没有形成规模，你可能会压垮一个组织，

turns.en: you can't suddenly give someone a hundred million dollars and think they're gonna be able to spend that money, so we have to build the infrastructure around the country. So places can absorb the kind of capital to do things nationally. I think right now there is this sort of understanding of the wealth gap in this country,
turns.zh: 你不能突然给某人一亿美元，就以为他们能把这笔钱花好。所以我们必须在全国各地建立基础设施。好让各个地方能够吸收那种资本，去做全国性的事情。我认为，眼下有这样一种认识：这个国家的财富差距

turns.en: getting larger and larger and larger. And that is to me undermining philanthropy in a way that I think folks are thinking, well, you're giving away five percent of your wealth, but look what's happening and look how it's growing. I know that folks are much more serious about giving away their money right now at numbers that aren't limited
turns.zh: 正在变得越来越大、越来越大。而对我来说，这在某种程度上正在削弱 philanthropy，人们会想，嗯，你捐出你财富的 5%，可看看正在发生的事、看看这个差距增长得有多快。我知道，现在人们对捐钱这件事认真得多，捐出的数额不再受某个百分比的限制。

turns.en: by some percentage. They're not saying I'm giving this away because it's the IRS law. They're saying I'm giving this away because I feel like I have an obligation to this country to give more. Those are the folks who are joining the Blue Meridian Partners Group that I know of. And Michael and Susan Dell came to me and said,
turns.zh: 他们不是在说，'我捐这个是因为 IRS 的法律'。他们是在说，'我捐这个是因为我觉得，我对这个国家有一份义务，要捐得更多。'这些正是加入我所了解的 Blue Meridian Partners 团体的人。而 Michael 和 Susan Dell 来找我，说，

turns.en: if you get this law passed, if you can get this passed, you solve one of our biggest problems. We wanna give away all of our money and public reports, they have $200 billion. We wanna give all of our money away within 10 years of us passing away. The interesting thing about America, for all of its failings,
turns.zh: '如果你能让这部法律通过，如果你能推动它通过，你就解决了我们最大的难题之一。我们想把我们所有的钱都捐出去'——据公开报道，他们有 $2,000 亿。'我们想在我们去世后 10 年之内，把我们所有的钱都捐出去。'有趣的是，America 尽管有种种失败之处，

turns.en: it's the most giving country on the planet. You go to India, you go to Asia, you go to Africa, you go to Europe, it's about how they build dynastic wealth that they never give away. This country has a unique attribute that people wanna give all the money away. The problem was there was no philanthropic platform to give it away, right?
turns.zh: 它却是这个星球上最乐于捐赠的国家。你去 India、去 Asia、去 Africa、去 Europe，那里讲的是他们如何积累那种永远不捐出去的'世代财富'。这个国家有一种独特的特质：人们想把钱全都捐出去。问题是，过去没有一个慈善平台能让你把钱捐出去，对吧？

turns.en: Now we have created the largest platform for direct giving in the history of the world. If you wanna give away $10 billion like Elon or six and a half like the Dell's, like that, one page donor agreement with the US Treasury, and then you wire them the money and they wired out to the kids. That's why Michael has called this
turns.zh: 现在，我们创建了世界历史上最大的直接捐赠平台。如果你想捐出 $100 亿，像 Elon 那样，或者 $65 亿，像 Dell（夫妇）那样，只需与 US Treasury 签一页纸的捐赠协议，然后你把钱汇给他们，他们再汇给那些孩子。这就是为什么 Michael 把这称为、

turns.en: and I've called it Giving Pledge 2.0, right? We're narrowing the gap between the pledge and the giving, right? It happens at the same time. And so to me, I think you're going to see these folks give away a lot more than has been announced. I'm in the room having the conversations with the people that the Jeffrey works with.
turns.zh: 而我把这称为'Giving Pledge 2.0'，对吧？我们在缩小'承诺'与'实际捐赠'之间的差距，对吧？它们同时发生。所以，在我看来，我认为你会看到这些人捐出远比已经宣布的要多得多的钱。我就在那个房间里，跟那些与 Jeffrey 共事的人进行着这些对话。

turns.en: They all wanna do this. So if they wanna adopt the two million kids in the city of New York, just call me up. It's a, we'll white glove it with the US Treasury Department. It's a one page pledge. You can give $500 bucks to all the kids in New York City or in San Francisco, like I said, like Neil Meta just announced yesterday,
turns.zh: 他们都想做这件事。所以，如果他们想'认领'New York City 里那两百万个孩子，尽管打电话给我。我们会跟 US Treasury Department 一起，把这件事'白手套'式地办得妥妥帖帖。这是一页纸的承诺。你可以给 New York City 的所有孩子每人 $500，或者像我说的那样，在 San Francisco——就像 Neil Meadow 昨天刚刚宣布的，

turns.en: a hundred bucks to all the kids in San Francisco. We've unlocked this power of philanthropy and I know that you've shared this with me. Folks that are already on the forefront of this, Harlem Children's Zone, Blue Meridian, Stan Drucken Miller, when they heard about this, they were the first ones to call me and say, is it true?
turns.zh: 给 San Francisco 的所有孩子每人 $100。我们已经释放了 philanthropy 的这股力量。而且我知道，你也跟我分享过这一点：那些已经站在这件事最前沿的人——Harlem Children's Zone、Blue Meridian、Stan Druckenmiller——当他们听说了这件事，他们是第一批打电话给我、说'这是真的吗？

turns.en: Tell us that it's true. Tell us that these universal capital accounts are gonna be here forever because if they are, then the $25 trillion of wealth in the United States that's gonna change hands over the course of the next 10 to 15 years, you're gonna see 10 or 20% of that go directly into these kids accounts and that's when we changed
turns.zh: 告诉我们这是真的'的人。告诉我们这些全民资本账户会永远存在。因为如果它们会永远存在，那么 America 那 $25 万亿的财富——在未来 10 到 15 年间将会易手的财富——你会看到其中的 10% 或 20% 直接流入这些孩子的账户。而那时，我们就永远地改变了

turns.en: the country forever. You're gonna scale up the capital in every one of these accounts and now we have everybody in the game. I think this is one of the most profound ways of impacting poverty that I have seen in my more than 50 years being involved in education. It's an opportunity I thought we would never have.
turns.zh: 这个国家。你会把每一个这样的账户里的资本都做大，这下我们让所有人都参与到这场游戏里了。我认为，这是他投身教育事业 50 多年来所见证过的、最深刻的能够影响贫困的方式之一。这是一个我原以为我们永远不会拥有的机会。

turns.en: I didn't think we could ever get this thing scaled in the way that Brad has been able to do and I think it would be a mistake not to use this to actually create the next generation of capitalists in this country who will mostly be poor people. Wouldn't that be amazing? I mean, it would just be stunning if you looked around
turns.zh: 我没想到我们能把这件事规模化，做到 Brad 所做到的那种程度；而我认为，如果不用它来真正地创造这个国家下一代的资本家——他们大多数将会是穷人——那将是一个错误。那难道不令人惊叹吗？我是说，如果你环顾四周，看到

turns.en: and like, wow, there's more of them than there is of us which is flipping this thing on its head right now and I just think that's gonna be the new invention in this country that we're gonna create a new economic model that really has all of us rooting for the success of business, rooting for the success of our country,
turns.zh: '哇，他们的人数比我们还多'，从而把整个局面彻底颠覆，那就太惊人了。我只是觉得，那将会是这个国家的'新发明'：我们将创造一种新的经济模式，它真正让我们所有人都为商业的成功加油、为我们国家的成功加油，

turns.en: feeling like we're all in this game and we all have a huge upside. I learned when I was young in communication that the key is, tell them what you're gonna tell them, tell them and then tell them that you told them. You gotta repeat things for them to land and so I wanna as we wind down, I wanna ask you, Jeffrey, especially to repeat
turns.zh: 感觉到我们都在这场游戏里、都有着巨大的上升空间。我年轻时在沟通方面学到，关键就是：先告诉他们你要讲什么，然后讲给他们听，然后再告诉他们你刚才讲了什么。你得把事情重复，它们才能落地。所以，在我们收尾的时候，我想请 Jeffrey，特别是，把你

turns.en: sort of the summary of everything that you've said so far. If I ask you to sort of dream about what is now possible because of this technology, this structure, this infrastructure and summarize the problem first that it might help alleviate or significantly help alleviate. Maybe just close this down with,
turns.zh: 迄今所说的一切做个总结、再重复一遍。如果我请你畅想一下，因为有了这项技术、这套结构、这套基础设施，如今有什么变得可能了；并先把那个问题总结一下——它也许能帮助缓解、或显著帮助缓解（那个问题）。也许就这样收尾吧，

turns.en: you're such a passionate guy, it's amazing to listen to you talk. Maybe just do it for us one more time about what's at stake and what might happen. Here's one of the big challenges I think in our country. I have, as many Republican friends, as if I have Democratic friends, both sides really love this country for real. I mean for real.
turns.zh: 你是如此有激情的一个人，听你讲话太棒了。也许就再为我们讲一遍，讲讲这里头的利害所在、以及可能发生什么。这里有一个我认为我们国家面临的大挑战。我有同样多的 Republican 朋友，就像我有一样多的 Democratic 朋友，两边都真正热爱这个国家，是认真的。我是说，认真的。

turns.en: And both sides think the other side really doesn't love America in the same way and it's not true. I feel right now as a country we're at an inflection point like that, the system has broken down and folks don't realize it because if you're a privileged person like me, you don't feel it.
turns.zh: 而两边都以为，另一边并不像自己这样、以同样的方式真正热爱 America，而这是不实的。我此刻感觉到，作为一个国家，我们正处在一个拐点，就像，这个制度已经崩坏，而人们没有意识到，因为如果你是一个像我这样的特权阶层，你感觉不到它。

turns.en: And if you live in certain places, you don't see it. When I'm with my kids and I'm traveling around this country, I'm hearing from folks. This thing is not working. I've tried and I've tried. I can't make it work. And not just me, it's my kids. It's education systems failing them. There are no jobs out there for them.
turns.zh: 而如果你住在某些地方，你也看不到它。当我跟我的孩子们一起、走遍这个国家时，我在听人们说，'这个东西不管用。我试过又试过。我没法让它运转起来。而且不只是我，还有我的孩子。是教育系统在辜负他们。外面根本没有适合他们的工作。

turns.en: They close the factories, they close the mines. We don't know what to do. What is our future in this place right now? We don't have a clue. And we're looking for someone, the whole responsible, point me to the villain. Is it the immigrants? Is it these folks who are the villains destroying my life in America?
turns.zh: 他们关掉了工厂，关掉了矿井。我们不知道该怎么办。此刻，我们在这个地方的未来是什么？我们一点头绪都没有。'而我们在寻找某个人、某个该负责的对象，'给我指认那个恶棍。是移民吗？是这些正在摧毁我在 America 生活的人吗，他们是恶棍吗？'

turns.en: And we know it is not any of those groups. We have created a system that for this moment, it's simply not working for America's. I think the way we engage Americans back is the same thing that drove that mother to leave her house at five o'clock in the morning and work all day. And some kitchen is some. She did it for her kids.
turns.zh: 而我们知道，那不是他们中的任何一群。是我们创造了一个制度，在这个时刻，它对 America 的这些人就是不管用。我认为，我们让美国人重新参与进来的方式，跟当年驱使那位母亲清晨五点离开家、在某个厨房里干上一整天活的那种动力是一样的。她是为了她的孩子才这么做的。

turns.en: And if you ask her why she would do it, she did it for her kids. And she didn't say, you know what, I think that this system is failed. She thought the system is working because my kids are going to school. They don't get education. They will never have to come in here and slave like I'm saving right now.
turns.zh: 而如果你问她为什么要这样，她是为了她的孩子。她并没有说，'你知道吗，我觉得这个制度失败了。'她觉得这个制度是管用的，因为我的孩子能上学、能受教育。他们将永远不必像我此刻这样，进来当牛做马。

turns.en: And for that, I work and I give my labor. When that doesn't work anymore and it's not working anywhere in the country, when that doesn't work anymore, and I'm still out there breaking my back and my kids are doing worse. They're actually doing worse than then you feel like the system has failed. And you know what, it has. It has.
turns.zh: 而为了这个，我工作、我付出我的劳动。'当这一切不再管用时——而它在全国各地都不再管用时——当这一切不再管用了，而我仍然在外面拼命干活、我的孩子却过得更糟，他们实际上过得比那时更糟，你就会觉得这个制度失败了。而且你知道吗，它确实失败了。它确实失败了。

turns.en: We need to reinvent a way to get Americans invested in the future of this country. And the way you do it's get them to know their kids are going to benefit. And I think all of us who have kids, I think we're willing to sacrifice whatever we need if we think our kids are going to make it. But if my kid is not going to make it,
turns.zh: 我们需要重新发明一种方式，让美国人对这个国家的未来有所投入。而你做到这一点的方式，就是让他们知道，他们的孩子将会受益。我想，我们所有有孩子的人，如果我们觉得我们的孩子能出头，我们愿意牺牲任何需要牺牲的东西。但如果我的孩子出不了头，

turns.en: don't have me out here losing my health and other stuff. And my kid, I know doesn't have a chance. Now I'm looking for something to break down the system to burn it down. I'm not, you know what, Americans are funny. We can take a lot, but we reach a breaking point. I stand, Dr. Miller, who's our board chair
turns.zh: 就别让我在这儿赔上健康之类的东西，而我还明知我的孩子没有机会。现在，我就要去找点能把这个制度砸烂、把它烧掉的东西了。我不是……你知道吗，美国人很有意思。我们能忍很多，但我们终会到达一个爆发点。我（要提）Stan Druckenmiller，他是我们的董事会主席，

turns.en: and my dear friend, best friend. Him and I about eight years ago, we went around a country talking about generational theft. We thought we could start a movement saying we created these things for old people. So they could never be poor. Social security, Medicare and Medicaid, right? We took all the money from the young people
turns.zh: 也是我亲爱的朋友、最好的朋友。大约八年前，他和我一起走遍全国，谈论'世代盗窃'（generational theft）。我们原以为能掀起一场运动，指出：我们为老年人创造了这些东西，好让他们永远不会贫穷——Social Security、Medicare 和 Medicaid，对吧？我们把所有的钱从年轻人那里拿来，

turns.en: to give it to them. To give it to us. And we didn't mean to test it. So Stan is getting social security. He was like, that's crazy. And you can't change it. And we thought we could start a movement in America. Because once we exposed it, we went to college campus after college campus saying, hey guys, we need to rethink this and reinvest
turns.zh: 来给他们。来给我们。而我们并非有意'检验'它。所以 Stan 现在领着 Social Security。他当时说，'那太疯狂了。'而你没法改变它。我们原以为能在 America 掀起一场运动。因为一旦我们把它揭露出来——我们去了一个又一个大学校园，说，嘿，各位，我们需要重新思考这件事，并重新投资

turns.en: in America's children. Here he is, one of the biggest philanthropists of Republican, I'm a Democrat. We're out together saying something is broken in our country. And we need to fix it. It didn't catch on. We did a lot of work. We went a lot of places. We couldn't get enough rising. Brand has created a way for us to go back and say,
turns.zh: 于 America 的孩子们。瞧他，是 Republican 里最大的慈善家之一，而我是 Democrat。我们俩一起出去，说我们这个国家有东西坏掉了。我们需要修好它。它没有流行起来。我们做了很多工作。我们去了很多地方。却没法激起足够的共鸣。而 Brad 创造了一种方式，让我们能回过头去说——

turns.en: his generational theft in reverse. That's told of us old folks. Give back to our young people. Let's do it at scale in a way that's going to be transformative in this country. That's what this moment is about to me. I have goosebumps literally sitting here because I know what we're going to do together over the next decade, right?
turns.zh: 这是'反过来的世代盗窃'。这是对我们这些老家伙说的：回馈给我们的年轻人吧。让我们以一种规模化的、将在这个国家带来变革的方式去做。这就是这个时刻对我而言的意义。我坐在这儿真的起了鸡皮疙瘩，因为我知道，未来十年我们要一起做些什么，对吧？

turns.en: This has been, you know, this is the dream, but also kind of the hurt that you can only have having this lived experience. You know, my mom worked two jobs. And then we'd come home. She couldn't afford to go to college, even though she was really smart, but she dreamed of me being able to go to college.
turns.zh: 这一直是，你知道，这既是那个梦想，也是那种只有拥有这段亲身经历才会有的伤痛。你知道，我妈妈打两份工。然后我们（才）回到家。她上不起大学，尽管她真的很聪明，但她梦想着我能上大学。

turns.en: But we couldn't afford to pay for me to go to college. So I remember sitting with her at a typewriter while she helps me with my college application. And the only schools I applied to are schools that could give me a full scholarship. So that I could go and begin the journey for our family to put it back on its feet, right?
turns.zh: 但我们付不起我上大学的钱。所以我记得和她一起坐在打字机前，她帮我弄我的大学申请。而我申请的唯一那些学校，都是能给我全额奖学金的学校，好让我能去上大学、开启这段旅程，让我们的家庭重新站起来，对吧？

turns.en: She never lost faith. But when you lose faith, it's desperate, right? I am equally concerned, but I'm even more optimistic. Because when I set out on this journey five years ago, Jeffrey, everybody said it can't be done. We're Republicans and Democrats will never agree. But the thing about this country, it has a unique DNA, OK?
turns.zh: 她从未失去信心。但当你失去信心时，那是绝望的，对吧？我同样担忧，但我甚至更乐观。因为当我五年前踏上这段旅程时，Jeffrey，每个人都说不可能做成。'Republicans 和 Democrats 永远不会达成一致。'但这个国家的特质在于，它有一种独特的 DNA，好吗？

turns.en: Our first advantage is we have the most invention. We have the greatest economy. We have the greatest entrepreneurs. We have the greatest system of risk capital. We are going to create more abundance than any other country on the planet by a long shot. And it's happening at an accelerating rate. That is America's great advantage.
turns.zh: 我们的首要优势是，我们拥有最多的发明。我们有最伟大的经济。我们有最伟大的企业家。我们有最伟大的风险资本体系。我们将创造的丰饶，会比这个星球上任何其他国家都多得多，而且差距悬殊。它正以加速的速度发生。这是 America 的伟大优势。

turns.en: We do not have an abundance problem. We do not have an invention problem. We have a distribution problem, right? The distribution of the winnings is too concentrated among the wealthy. And the temptation is therefore to attack the wealthy, to attack success, to attack capitalism, and to throw it out. That would be killing the golden goose
turns.zh: 我们并没有丰饶不足的问题。我们也没有发明不足的问题。我们有一个分配问题，对吧？收益的分配在富人当中太过集中。因此，诱惑就是去攻击富人、攻击成功、攻击资本主义，把它整个扔掉。那等于杀死了那只下金蛋的鹅——

turns.en: that creates the prosperity and the abundance in the first place, right? The way in which we do this is we harness the power of that abundance, of the coming prosperity that's coming from this invention, and we get everybody into the game. And I thought to it may be impossible, but it wasn't impossible.
turns.zh: 正是它一开始创造了繁荣与丰饶，对吧？我们这样做的方式，是驾驭那种丰饶的力量、驾驭这场即将到来的、源自发明的繁荣，让所有人都参与到这场游戏里。而我原以为，这也许是不可能的，但它并非不可能。

turns.en: And for whatever you want to say about this president, right? I told him, when I had the opportunity in the Oval Office, I said, if you believe in the Main Street Agenda, this is your Main Street Agenda. Every kid in America sharing in the upside of the prosperity that we're going to create.
turns.zh: 而不管你想怎么评价这位总统，对吧？当我有机会在 Oval Office 里时，我告诉他，我说，如果你相信 Main Street Agenda，那这就是你的 Main Street Agenda。让 America 的每一个孩子，都分享我们将要创造的繁荣的收益。

turns.en: And he was a one, and it took a unique entrepreneurial courage to get that done. Now, we had tons of democratic support. Tons of Republican support who also wanted this to happen. That's why I'm so optimistic. Jeffrey, we did it. We have the universal Republicans. We have 70 million accounts. No other country on the planet is doing this.
turns.zh: 而他全力以赴，要促成这件事需要一种独特的、企业家式的勇气。现在，我们有大量 Democratic 的支持。大量 Republican 的支持，他们也想要这件事发生。这就是为什么我如此乐观。Jeffrey，我们做到了。我们有了这些普及全民的（账户）。我们有了 7,000 万个账户。这个星球上没有别的国家在做这件事。

turns.en: And by the way, no other country on the planet has the economy that can afford to do this. So we again are back in a unique position. This is 1935 America, but way better. OK? We have a new social contract that everybody has included in capital that will compound from birth. We need to double down on this.
turns.zh: 而顺便说一句，这个星球上也没有别的国家，拥有那种负担得起做这件事的经济体。所以，我们又一次处在了一个独特的位置。这是 1935 年的 America，但好得多。好吗？我们有了一份新的社会契约，每个人都被纳入资本之中，那资本将从出生起就复利增长。我们需要在这件事上加码。

turns.en: We need to get everybody in, you know, aware of it in the game, claiming their accounts enthusiastic about it. And then we need to let our thoroughbreds run. We need to let capitalism be the great force that Keynes told us 100 years ago it would be, and it was. OK? That's the agenda. That's the mission for the next 100 years.
turns.zh: 我们需要让每个人都进来、你知道，了解它、参与到游戏里、认领他们的账户、对它充满热情。然后，我们需要让我们的'纯种赛马'（thoroughbreds）尽情奔跑。我们需要让资本主义成为 Keynes 一百年前告诉我们的那股伟大力量——而它确实是。好吗？这就是议程。这就是未来 100 年的使命。

turns.en: We just need to make sure we solve the distribution problem and that everybody else is in the game and feels like they're in the game. And I'll just say, Patrick, I told us, I wasn't down with capitalism until I got some capital. I was just being honest. And I was like, no one told me about this. How could this thing go on? It is funny.
turns.zh: 我们只需要确保解决分配问题，让其他所有人都参与到这场游戏里、并感觉到自己参与其中。我就说一句，Patrick，我告诉过大家，在我拿到一些资本之前，我压根不待见资本主义。我只是实话实说。我当时就想，没人跟我讲过这个啊，这东西（怎么一直）运转下去的？这很有意思。

turns.en: There is no one that I knew growing up, or in my thousands and thousands of kids who have any capital. None. None. They're all negative. They're all got credit cards with too much debt on it. And they don't get it. It's not real to them. So why wouldn't you get rid of it? It doesn't even exist.

turns.zh: 而尽管我为这场对话如此兴奋，我也相当期待问 Jeffrey 这个问题：别人为你做过的最善良的一件事是什么？改变我一生的，是我读高中三年级的时候。我的社会研究老师和她的丈夫，组织了一趟去 Europe 的旅行，去 Europe 七个国家，为那些富人家的孩子。

turns.en: And they had the idea that, well, we shouldn't invite, and then I was in a poor high school. We shouldn't invite a couple of poor kids, and we should get a scholarship for them. turns.zh: 去拥有一段经历。（它）改变了我的人生，把我送上了一条完全不同的轨迹。我甚至不知道那个人是谁。我不知道他为什么这么做。他为我做了这件事。我只是觉得，那份礼物——把那份改变了我人生的礼物回报出去——即便以我所做的一切，我仍然觉得我做得还不够。
